text:
I

The sun of fortune

has not yet given my eyes

your image; my cravings

perceive your beauty,

perceive on high

the gleam of an angel,

the beautiful face of a fairy...

To call my sad fate happy,

angel, fairy, or woman, I long to see you.


II

Love inspires me, the bird

messenger of the air,

that carries to the high sphere

like a heavenly ship

love's gentle song;

love also inspires me,

the flower that breathes aroma,

and such joy your name pours into my being,

that flower, bird, or woman, I die to see you.


III

I do not know if you are a morning star

that announces a joyful day,

or in shadowy storm

offers a course

to the sad sailor;

yet angel or fairy,

or precious bird or flower,

or magic star;

to love life more than death,

my longing, lady, is to know you.

translation.title: The Sun of Fortune...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the three-part courtly ascent through angel, fairy, bird, flower, and star.
